title: When a New Faith Crosses the Halfway Mark — Austronesian Conversion Clocks, Bass Diffusion Math, Political Authority & Archival Thresholds

teenKit.tldr: How does an entire society completely flip its worldview, traditions, and beliefs in just 25 years instead of centuries? This episode investigates the math, friction, and historical clues behind how fast new ideas swallow a culture.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how rapidly belief systems spread unlocks the mechanics of viral trends, social movements, and how human communities collectively change their minds.
keyTakeaways: Cultural and religious worldview shifts are not always glacial; they can completely overhaul a society in a single generation.
Researchers use quantitative tools like Bass Diffusion Math to model and track the speed of human behavioral change.
Historians piece together messy archival evidence—like old sailors' journals and land deeds—to watch these massive human transitions through a foggy lens.

A mathematical model used to predict how new products, ideas, or behaviors spread through a population over time.
The organized power and leadership structures that heavily influence or accelerate community-wide decisions.
The specific limits and tipping points of historical evidence found in old documents that let researchers piece together past events.
